title: Internal Hom with an invertible twist
statement:
Let $p,\ell$ be distinct primes and let $a,N\geq1$ be integers. Put $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$. Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite extension with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, put $A_{E,N}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^N$, and choose $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,N},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. Fix a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum] on separated finite-type $k$-schemes and let $X$ be a scheme in this datum. Let $K,M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$, with $K$ perfect over its coefficient unit $\Lambda_X$: locally on the coefficient site it is isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite projective $\Lambda_X$-modules, as in [def-weil-site-perfect-complex]. Let $m,r\in\mathbf Z$. Use the coefficient operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and put $K^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\Lambda_X)$. The twist $\Lambda(m)_X$ is the object of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. It is invertible: at finite coefficients it is a locally constant rank-one sheaf; at integral coefficients it is a locally free rank-one module over the completed coefficient sheaf; at $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ it is the image of that integral line in the rationalized and common-finite-stage categories, respectively. The canonical map
$$
R\mathcal Hom_X(K,M\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}\Lambda(m)_X)\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_X(K,M)\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}\Lambda(m)_X
$$
is an isomorphism. Here this arrow is the inverse of the evaluation comparison $c_{M,\Lambda(m)_X}$, the tensor–Hom transpose of $\mathrm{ev}\otimes1$ in the opposite direction. In particular,
$$
R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\Lambda_X(m)[r])\cong K^\vee(m)[r].
$$

proof.text: Put $L=\Lambda(m)_X$ and write $\otimes$ for the specified derived tensor. Apply [prop-weil-twist-preserves] with $S=X$. Its coefficient rings and twists are exactly those of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], since $\ell\ne p$ is invertible on the schemes in [def-sf-datum]. It gives the finite rank-one locally constant line, the integral rank-one line over the completed coefficient sheaf, and the invertible images at the two field stages. It also gives the inverse twist $(-)(-m)$ and preservation of $D^b_{ctf}$ at every stage. The unit $\Lambda_X$ is an object of $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ and $\Lambda_X(m)=\Lambda_X\otimes^L L\cong L$ by the unit isomorphism of the tensor of sheaf complexes, so $L$ and every $M(m)$ lie in $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$. At finite coefficients the specified tensor of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] is the derived tensor used in [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], so $M\otimes L=M(m)$. At integral coefficients the specified tensor is the completed tensor $\widehat\otimes$, whereas the twist $M(m)=M\otimes^L_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}}L$ is the ordinary ambient tensor of the ringed site. Since $X$ is separated of finite type over $k$, it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and $M,L\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$; hence [lem-fix-constructible-tensor-completion] gives the canonical natural isomorphism $\chi_{M,L}:M(m)\xrightarrow{\sim}M\mathbin{\widehat\otimes}L$. At $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ both the operations and the twists are formed on integral representatives, so the same comparison applies. Thus $M\otimes L\cong M(m)$ lies in the required coefficient category, and the twist autoequivalence is the specified one, not tensoring with a discrete constant integral or rational sheaf.

source.place: First sentence: coefficient twists are invertible lines; use the existing twist-preservation theorem for the precise coefficient-dependent assertion.

proof.text:
The perfect object $K$ in the coefficient category of the datum satisfies the local bounded finite-projective hypothesis of [prop-sf-dualizable-hom], by [def-weil-site-perfect-complex]. All operations are those of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], including completed integral tensor and the field-stage conventions. For $Q=M$ and $Q=M\otimes L$, the latter being in $D^b_{ctf}$ by step 1, that proposition gives the canonical evaluation isomorphisms $a_Q:K^\vee\otimes Q\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_X(K,Q)$. Consequently the composite
$$
b=(a_M\otimes1_L)\circ\alpha^{-1}\circ a_{M\otimes L}^{-1}:R\mathcal Hom_X(K,M\otimes L)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_X(K,M)\otimes L
$$
is an isomorphism, where $\alpha:(K^\vee\otimes M)\otimes L\xrightarrow{\sim}K^\vee\otimes(M\otimes L)$ is tensor reassociation. This is precisely the perfect-duality route in the last part of the blueprint proof.

source.place: Sentence beginning For K perfect: apply the coefficient-dual tensor comparison twice and reassociate.

proof.text:
It remains to identify $b$ with the displayed canonical arrow. Let $c_{M,L}:R\mathcal Hom_X(K,M)\otimes L\to R\mathcal Hom_X(K,M\otimes L)$ be the transpose of $\mathrm{ev}\otimes1_L$. The canonical evaluation comparisons of [prop-sf-dualizable-hom] satisfy
$$
c_{M,L}\circ(a_M\otimes1_L)=a_{M\otimes L}\circ\alpha.
$$
Indeed, after tensoring with $K$ and evaluating, both sides contract the same factors $K^\vee\otimes K\to\Lambda_X$ and leave $M\otimes L$ unchanged; the associators and symmetry only put these factors in this order. This checks equality by the definition of the tensor–Hom transpose, with the same Koszul symmetry on both sides. At integral coefficients the comparison $\chi$ of [lem-fix-constructible-tensor-completion] identifies the completed tensor on these objects with the ordinary tensor of the ringed site, so the transposes are the ordinary tensor–Hom transposes there; at the field stages the same identities hold after scalar localization and passage to a common stage. Since both $a$ maps and $\alpha$ are invertible, the equation gives $c_{M,L}=b^{-1}$. Therefore the canonical arrow in the statement, its inverse, is the isomorphism $b$. No generator argument or identification with a small-etale abstract Tate object is used.

source.place: Definition of c as transpose of evaluation, and the final perfect-duality sentence: identify the two canonical maps explicitly.

proof.text: For the last assertion note $\Lambda_X(m)[r]\cong L[r]$ by step 1 and take $Q=L[r]$ in [prop-sf-dualizable-hom]; the line and its shift are in $D^b_{ctf}$ by step 1 and the triangulated-category convention in [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. This gives $R\mathcal Hom_X(K,L[r])\cong K^\vee\otimes L[r]$. Tensor with a shifted second factor identifies the latter with $(K^\vee\otimes L)[r]$. At finite coefficients, let $P$ be a K-flat representative of $K^\vee$ as used to compute the derived tensor in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and regard $L$ as the degree-zero line. With the total-tensor differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and the convention $d_{C[r]}=(-1)^r d_C$, this chain identification multiplies the summand $P^i\otimes L$ by $(-1)^{ri}$: the target differential on that summand is $(-1)^r d_P$, so $(-1)^{r(i+1)}d_P=(-1)^r d_P(-1)^{ri}$. It is its own inverse. At integral coefficients the same formula is compatible with all finite reductions in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; the shifted-cone limit construction commutes with the fixed shift and these maps. More explicitly, products commute with the shift by reindexing degrees, and with the convention $\operatorname{Cone}(f)=B\oplus A[1]$ the map $\operatorname{Cone}(f[r])\to\operatorname{Cone}(f)[r]$ is $(b,a)\mapsto(b,(-1)^r a)$; substituting in the cone differential checks the chain-map identity. Applying the outer shift $[-1]$ gives the comparison for the specified derived-limit complex. Rationalizing and representing at a common finite field preserves these isomorphisms. Finally $(K^\vee\otimes L)[r]\cong K^\vee(m)[r]$. At finite coefficients this is the definition in [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. At integral coefficients, and hence on the integral representatives used at the field stages, it is the inverse of the comparison $\chi_{K^\vee,L}$ of [lem-fix-constructible-tensor-completion], applied to $K^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\Lambda_X)$ as the object of $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ on which the completed tensor of [prop-sf-dualizable-hom] is formed for $Q=\Lambda_X$ (the displayed integral operations are taken on $D^b_c$), and to $L\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ from step 1; the twist itself is the ordinary tensor of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed].

source.place: Last sentence: the coefficient-dual case, with the shift and its chain sign written explicitly.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q38-4df4fb7bf (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the full mathematics against master and main-20261015 and every cited statement. The statement is not weakened. It spells out the six-functor datum's parameters, keeps K perfect in D^b_ctf (the same domain as prop-sf-dualizable-hom), and states the line clause in its exact form for each coefficient stage: locally free rank one over the completed sheaf at integral level, which matches def-coefficient-twists-detailed and prop-weil-twist-preserves. It names the arrow as c^{-1}, as in the main-20261015 unit proof. Steps 2-3: prop-sf-dualizable-hom applies to Q=M and Q=M(x)L. The identity c(a_M(x)1)=a_{M(x)L}alpha is a closed-monoidal coherence, so marking it elementary is acceptable. Step 4: I checked the sign (-1)^{ri} and the cone map (b,a)->(b,(-1)^r a). I tested m=0, m<0, r=0, r<0, K=0, M=0 and X empty. There are no new nodes and no duplicates; the imported general sk-lem-sf-twist-interchange node is in a different, unbridged category. Fault repaired (C1/C4): at integral level, step 1 treats M(x)L=M(m) and step 4 treats K^vee(x)L[r]=K^vee(m)[r] as holding by definition. But the datum's tensor is the completed derived-limit tensor, while the twist is the ordinary ringed-site tensor over the completed sheaf. The existing reviewed lem-fix-constructible-tensor-completion supplies the isomorphism chi: X is qcqs and M, L are in D^b_c. I cited it in steps 1, 3 and 4, added the unit identification Lambda_X(m)=L, and updated proof_deps. Accepted tool_uses: prop-weil-twist-preserves (declared by the worker) and lem-fix-constructible-tensor-completion (added by me in split_report.tool_uses); neither reaches the item, so there is no cycle. The unit's realized fields are correct.
